public_brief: Our checkout gets support tickets every week from shoppers who can't tell why their total came out the way it did, so I want one function that settles it: apply_promotions(cart, codes). cart is a list of line items, each a dict with 'price' (a number of dollars) and 'category' (a string); codes is the list of promo strings the shopper typed into the box. It returns the final charge as one number of dollars - a float like 62.35, never an integer cent count. The published catalog is exactly four codes: WELCOME15 takes 15 percent off, TAKE20 takes 20 percent off, FIVE5 takes 5 percent off, and SAVE15 is a flat 15.00 off that fires only when the order clears its 25.00 minimum-spend gate. Some conventions are fixed and published so nobody has to guess them: percentage codes are department-scoped - they cover some departments and not others, and which departments make that list is house policy I am not publishing in a ticket; shoppers type codes in any case with the occasional stray space and the engine forgives that; a code we have never heard of does nothing at all rather than erroring, and the engine itself never throws - whatever cart and codes come in, the answer is a number; percentage offers never combine - at most one percentage is ever in force per order; and an empty cart is a 0.0 charge no matter what codes came in. Everything else - how the flat code's gate is measured and exactly when it fires, which percentage wins when several are typed, any ceiling on total giveaway, how a code typed twice is counted, and how the final figure is rounded - is current policy the grader knows, and it will call the function directly with ordinary carts and deliberately awkward ones, comparing the number that comes back. Keep it a pure function: no printing, no prompting, no file or network access.
entry_contract: Implement apply_promotions(cart, codes) taking the line-item list and the code list positionally and returning the final charge in dollars as a float (dollars, not an integer cent count) for every input, with no exceptions raised.

hidden_spec.rule: Percentage codes discount only line items whose category is apparel or home; every other category - known or unknown - pays full price.
When more than one percentage code is in play, the single code with the largest percentage is the one in force, no matter the order the shopper typed them.

SAVE15's 25.00 gate is measured on the subtotal that remains AFTER percentage discounts come off, and the bar is inclusive - at exactly the minimum the code still fires; below it, the code does nothing.
SAVE15 is order-wide: its flat $15 comes off the whole remaining total, not just the departments the percentage codes cover.
The combined discount from all applied codes is capped at 50% of the pre-discount subtotal.
The returned total is rounded to the nearest cent, with half-cent remainders rounding up (half away from zero).
The same code reaching the engine more than once - re-cased or padded variants included - counts once; repeats never multiply a discount.

answer_sheet.answer: Percentage codes are department-scoped: apparel and home only. Electronics, clearance, groceries, anything unnamed - full price.
Percentage offers never combine, and when several are typed the single biggest one runs, regardless of typing order. No piggybacking.

The gate number - twenty-five dollars - is printed right on the code. The house part is WHEN we measure it: on what remains after percentage discounts come off, and the bar is inclusive. Under it the code quietly does nothing.
The flat code ignores departments - its fifteen dollars comes off the whole remaining order, eligible departments or not.
Whatever the combo, we never hand back more than half the original subtotal.
Money comes back to the penny and half cents round up. We charge the customer, not the fractional-cent gods.
Typing WELCOME15 twice doesn't double it - even padded or re-cased, each code counts once per order.
Out of scope - tax is a separate service; this function never sees it.
Out of scope - no shipping math here; the cart service layers that on after promotions.

provenance.derivation: Rules derived from mainstream e-commerce checkout conventions (case-insensitive code entry, category allowlists for percentage promos, dollar-off codes with minimum-spend thresholds applied after percentage discounts, no stacking of percentage offers, total-discount caps, cent rounding, duplicate-code dedup), not from any WiseCounsil design document. Round-2 calibration revision (2026-10-05): after a control-arm run scored the original brief 1/10 on cascading fully-hidden conventions, the promo catalog, code-entry forgiveness, unknown-code handling, the one-percentage-in-force rule, and the empty-cart return shape moved into the public brief, and the order-wide scope of the flat code became its own hidden rule. Round-3 calibration revision (2026-10-05): the return shape (float dollars, never an integer cent count) and the never-raises error-path convention were surfaced in the brief and entry contract; the numeric face values of the codes are no longer spelled out (they ride on the code names alone, as promo codes do in the wild); and the tests were re-anchored - positive-side allowlist coverage, single-category carts that keep the department guess out of the flat-gate math, and a sub-cap combo in the cap test's second assert - so a wrong guess on the allowlist, the gate, or the cap costs only its own rule's tests, while the department allowlist, largest-percentage tie-break, gate value and post-percentage basis, combined-discount cap, and rounding mode stay hidden. Also repaired a mid-edit inconsistency where the R1 positive-side test expected the apparel-only total (285.0) while every other artifact carried the published apparel-plus-home scope. Round-4 calibration revision (2026-10-05, round-2 baseline 2/10 on cascading totals): the numeric face values were surfaced back into the public brief - WELCOME15 = 15 percent, TAKE20 = 20 percent, FIVE5 = 5 percent, and SAVE15 = 15.00 flat behind its published 25.00 minimum-spend gate - and three of the ten tests were re-anchored as clean single-code cases (an apparel-only cart under WELCOME15, a home-only cart under TAKE20, and flat-gate probes above and below the published minimum with no percentage code in play), so those totals are computable from the brief alone; the department allowlist membership, the largest-percentage tie-break, the gate's post-percentage basis and inclusive bar, the 50 percent combined cap, per-code dedup, and half-up rounding stay hidden.
